title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a Fock space on a quantum processor, providing experimental evidence for non-equilibrium phases of matter.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic non-equilibrium phases, but heating from energy absorption poses a challenge. Stabilizing these phases is crucial for quantum applications.
method: The authors use a quantum processor to simulate a periodically driven system and observe the emergence of prethermalization and time-crystalline order, likely by measuring local observables and correlations over time.
result: They observe robust prethermal plateaus and signatures of time-crystalline order, indicating that these phases can be stabilized in a controllable quantum device.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum matter and may inform the design of quantum simulators and sensors.

title: Tight And Self-Testing Multipartite Quantum Bell Inequalities From The Renormalization Group
authors: Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Author(s): Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, and Miguel Navascués

Attempts to understand multipartite quantum nonlocality are thwarted by the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities (QBI) for systems composed of more than a few separate parties. In this Letter, we introduce the notion of tight connectors, a class of tensors which, if contracted according …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050204] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tight connectors to construct multipartite quantum Bell inequalities via renormalization group, enabling self-testing of quantum states.
motivation: Multipartite quantum nonlocality is hard to characterize due to the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities for many parties.
method: Defines tight connectors, tensors that when contracted yield valid quantum Bell inequalities, and uses renormalization group techniques to generate them.
result: Provides a systematic method to construct tight multipartite quantum Bell inequalities that are self-testing, with examples.
conclusion: Offers a new tool for studying multipartite nonlocality and self-testing, advancing quantum information theory.

title: Boosting Work Extraction In Quantum Batteries Via Continuous Environment Monitoring
authors: Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, And Marco G. Genoni
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, and Marco G. Genoni

During the charging process, interactions between a quantum battery and its charger generally generate quantum correlations, which may reduce the amount of work extractable from the battery alone. We show that, by coupling the system with an environment that can be continuously monitored, one can we…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050406] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous monitoring of the environment during quantum battery charging can enhance work extraction by mitigating detrimental correlations.
motivation: Quantum correlations generated during battery charging can reduce extractable work, posing a challenge for quantum battery performance.
method: The authors model a quantum battery coupled to a monitored environment and analyze how continuous monitoring affects the charging dynamics and work extraction.
result: They find that continuous monitoring can boost the amount of work extractable from the battery, counteracting the negative effects of correlations.
conclusion: Continuous environment monitoring offers a practical strategy to improve quantum battery efficiency, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Bottlenecks In Quantum Channels And Finite Temperature Phases Of Matter
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, And Vedika Khemani
abstract:
Author(s): Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, and Vedika Khemani

We prove an analog of the “bottleneck theorem,” well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel’s steady state, then states initialized on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050402] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a quantum analog of the bottleneck theorem for Markovian channels, linking spectral gaps to steady-state weights and applying it to finite-temperature phases of matter.
motivation: The bottleneck theorem is a fundamental tool for classical Markov chains, but its quantum analog was missing. Understanding bottlenecks in quantum channels is crucial for characterizing mixing times and relaxation dynamics in quantum systems.
method: The authors prove a quantum bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, showing that if two subspaces are separated by a region of low steady-state weight, then transitions between them are suppressed. They then apply this to finite-temperature phases, using it to bound relaxation times.
result: They establish a rigorous connection between the spectral gap of a quantum channel and the steady-state weights of subspaces, and demonstrate that this can be used to prove slow relaxation in certain finite-temperature phases, such as symmetry-broken phases.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for analyzing quantum channels and contributes to understanding the dynamical stability of quantum phases of matter, with implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Anticoncentration Is (Almost) All You Need
authors: Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, And Jonas Helsen
abstract:
Author(s): Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, and Jonas Helsen

Until very recently, it was generally believed that the (approximate) 2-design property is strictly stronger than anticoncentration of random quantum circuits, mainly because it was shown that the latter anticoncentrate in logarithmic depth, while the former generally need linear depth circuits. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050601] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that anticoncentration of random quantum circuits is almost sufficient for approximate 2-design behavior, challenging the previous belief that 2-designs are strictly stronger.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the relationship between anticoncentration and approximate 2-designs in random quantum circuits, which is fundamental for understanding quantum advantage and randomness generation.
method: They provide rigorous proofs and constructions demonstrating that circuits with anticoncentration can be efficiently converted into approximate 2-designs with minimal overhead.
result: They prove that anticoncentration implies approximate 2-design up to logarithmic factors in depth, and provide explicit circuit constructions achieving this.
conclusion: Anticoncentration is almost as powerful as 2-designs for practical purposes, simplifying the requirements for quantum information protocols.

title: Designing Generalized Elegant Bell Inequalities In Higher Dimensions From A Tsirelson Bound
authors: Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, Ilkwon Sohn, And Wonhyuk Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, IlKwon Sohn, and Wonhyuk Lee

Elegant Bell inequality is well known for its distinctive property, being maximally violated by maximal entanglement, mutually unbiased bases, and symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure elements. Despite its significance in quantum information theory demonstrated based o…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012217] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes elegant Bell inequalities to higher dimensions using a Tsirelson bound, providing new nonlocality criteria that are maximally violated by specific quantum states.
motivation: Elegant Bell inequalities are important for quantum information, but their generalization to higher dimensions is challenging. The authors aim to design new inequalities that retain the desirable properties of maximal violation by entangled states and mutually unbiased bases.
method: The authors construct generalized elegant Bell inequalities for higher-dimensional systems by leveraging the Tsirelson bound, which characterizes the maximum quantum violation of Bell inequalities. They likely use algebraic and numerical optimization techniques to derive the inequalities and their quantum violations.
result: The paper presents new Bell inequalities that are maximally violated by certain quantum states, demonstrating the existence of higher-dimensional analogues of the elegant Bell inequality. The violations are tied to mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of elegant Bell inequalities to higher dimensions, offering new tools for detecting and quantifying nonlocality, which is relevant for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Strongly Driven Cavity-quantum-electrodynamical–optomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, And Shingo Kono
abstract:
Author(s): Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, and Shingo Kono

Hybrid quantum systems harness the distinct advantages of different physical platforms, yet their integration is not always trivial due to potential incompatibilities in operational principles. Here, we theoretically propose and demonstrate a scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states usin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013724] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate non-Gaussian mechanical states in a strongly driven cavity-QED-optomechanical hybrid system.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combine advantages of different platforms, but integration can be challenging; generating non-Gaussian states is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a hybrid system where a cavity-QED system is coupled to a mechanical oscillator, using strong driving to induce nonlinear interactions.
result: They demonstrate that non-Gaussian mechanical states can be generated under realistic parameters, with potential for quantum state engineering.
conclusion: The scheme offers a viable route for creating non-classical states in hybrid systems, advancing quantum technology applications.

title: Spacetime Markov Length: A Diagnostic For Fault Tolerance Via Mixed-state Phases
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, and Timothy H. Hsieh

We establish a correspondence between the fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes experiencing measurement and physical errors and the mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension. Drawing from recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, this motivates a diagnos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045130] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes and mixed-state phases in one higher dimension, introducing a diagnostic called spacetime Markov length.
motivation: To understand fault tolerance in quantum error correction from the perspective of mixed-state phases of matter, potentially providing new insights and diagnostics.
method: The authors draw on recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter to define a spacetime Markov length and analyze its behavior for local stabilizer codes under measurement and physical errors.
result: They establish a correspondence between fault tolerance and mixed-state phases, and the spacetime Markov length serves as a diagnostic for fault tolerance.
conclusion: The work connects quantum error correction with mixed-state phases, offering a new tool for assessing fault tolerance and potentially guiding the design of more robust codes.

title: Conservative Dissipation Shapes Symmetry Breaking In Nonequilibrium Currents
authors: Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, and Daniel Maria Busiello

Most natural thermodynamic systems operate far from equilibrium, developing persistent currents and organizing into nonequilibrium stationary states (NESSs). Yet, the general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033126] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how conservative dissipation in nonequilibrium systems breaks equilibrium symmetries and shapes stationary probability distributions, providing a general framework for understanding symmetry breaking in NESSs.
motivation: Most natural systems operate far from equilibrium, yet general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain poorly understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on conservative dissipation, analyzing how it modifies the stationary distribution and induces symmetry breaking in nonequilibrium currents.
result: They derive conditions under which conservative dissipation leads to symmetry breaking and characterize the resulting nonequilibrium stationary states.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics by linking dissipation to symmetry breaking, with implications for the design and analysis of far-from-equilibrium systems.

title: Quantum Repeaters Based On Stationary And Flying Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qudits
authors: Stefan Häussler And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Häussler and Peter van Loock

There are various approaches to long-range quantum communication based on conceptually different forms of quantum repeaters. Here, we explore a quantum repeater scheme that employs quantum error correction (QEC) both on the flying (light) qubits and on the stationary (matter) qubits. The idea is to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033101] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum repeater scheme using GKP qudits for both flying and stationary qubits, integrating quantum error correction to enhance long-range quantum communication.
motivation: Long-range quantum communication requires repeaters to overcome loss and noise. Existing schemes often rely on either entanglement swapping or error correction, but combining both on flying and stationary qubits could improve performance.
method: The authors design a repeater architecture where GKP qudits are used for both light and matter qubits, employing quantum error correction to protect against loss and operational errors. They analyze the scheme's performance in terms of entanglement distribution rates and fidelity.
result: The scheme demonstrates improved repeater performance compared to approaches without integrated error correction, potentially enabling higher rates and longer distances for quantum key distribution and other quantum network applications.
conclusion: The proposed GKP-based repeater with error correction on both flying and stationary qubits is a promising approach for practical quantum networks, offering a path toward scalable long-distance quantum communication.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote nodes are coupled via a unidirectional channel, and use a feedback-like mechanism that mimics a squeezed environment to continuously stabilize the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, showing resilience against realistic imperfections such as loss and dephasing.
conclusion: The demonstrated autonomous stabilization technique offers a practical path for maintaining entanglement in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed quantum information processing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but current methods often require active control or suffer from losses. The authors aim to provide a simpler, autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir.
method: Two superconducting qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the dissipative dynamics lead to steady-state entanglement without active feedback.
result: The experiment demonstrates stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with the entanglement persisting over time and robust against certain imperfections. The scheme is fully autonomous and scalable.
conclusion: This work establishes a new paradigm for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially enabling high-throughput and low-complexity generation of remote entanglement.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging, especially for implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler approach using non-Abelian anyons.
method: They propose a scheme that temporarily moves quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logical gates, leveraging the properties of these phases for computation.
result: The method enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without the need for intricate braiding, potentially simplifying experimental realization.
conclusion: This work offers a promising path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers by using non-Abelian phases for gate implementation.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity of tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in quantum networks, it is crucial to have efficient spin-photon interfaces with strong coupling. This work aims to overcome previous limitations in coupling efficiency and coherence.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy (SnV) centers to them. They characterize the optical and spin properties, measuring the coherent cooperativity and spin coherence times.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the SnV center and the cavity, with preserved spin coherence, enabling efficient spin-photon entanglement.
conclusion: This platform is promising for scalable quantum networks, as it provides a robust spin-photon interface with high cooperativity, suitable for entanglement distribution and quantum repeaters.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a unified criterion for quantumness that recovers standard signatures while uncovering nonclassical features in seemingly classical processes, potentially enabling new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process theories and generalized probabilistic theories, analyzing individual quantum processes to define a boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior.
result: They demonstrate that many phenomena long thought classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties, and their rule recovers standard quantum signatures.
conclusion: The unified rule offers a new perspective on quantumness, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to convert common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing reconfigurable entangled states in many spin ensembles, with applications to quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: The authors aim to overcome the challenge of generating and stabilizing entanglement in large spin ensembles, which is crucial for quantum sensing and many-body physics, by exploiting dissipative processes that are typically considered detrimental.
method: They propose a scheme using a common cavity mode to mediate dissipative entanglement between many spin ensembles, leveraging engineered dissipation to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, and demonstrate reconfigurability by tuning system parameters.
result: The scheme enables robust generation of multipartite entangled states, including states useful for quantum-enhanced sensing, and can be extended to engineer topological many-body states, as shown through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to harness dissipation for quantum technology, offering a versatile platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics with spin ensembles coupled to cavities.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) offers potential for high secret key rates, but discrete modulation schemes often suffer from lower rates and lack of composable security proofs. The authors aim to bridge this gap by combining advanced modulation with new security analysis tools.
method: The authors propose a discrete-modulated CV-QKD protocol and provide a composable security proof using novel techniques, likely including entropy accumulation or other information-theoretic tools. They also optimize the modulation and detection parameters to maximize the secret key rate.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate for CV-QKD over fiber optics, demonstrating the practical viability of discrete-modulated CV-QKD with composable security.
conclusion: The work brings highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation by providing a secure and efficient CV-QKD protocol.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but traditional readout methods suffer from Purcell decay and trade-offs between speed and fidelity.
method: The authors propose a novel readout scheme that exploits nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the transmon and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive interaction while suppressing Purcell decay through a bandgap-like effect.
result: The architecture demonstrates fast readout with high fidelity and built-in Purcell protection, as shown in experiments or simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a promising solution for improving transmon readout performance, potentially benefiting quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited. The authors aim to extend single-shot correction to exotic topological orders, which are of fundamental interest.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes based on chiral color codes, leveraging the topological properties to enable single-shot error correction.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating a new capability in quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work introduces new quantum error-correcting codes that could serve as platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation, particularly for exotic topological phases.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol for preparing logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, targeting distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires high-fidelity entanglement between distant nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and resource-intensive to purify. The goal is to reduce the overhead of preparing logical Bell pairs for fault-tolerant operations.
method: The protocol uses entanglement distillation and quantum error correction to distill noisy physical Bell pairs into logical Bell pairs, optimized for low spacetime volume and 2D local connectivity, likely leveraging surface codes or similar topological codes.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pairs with significantly reduced spacetime cost compared to existing methods, and requires only 2D local device connectivity, making it practical for near-term distributed architectures.
conclusion: This work provides a resource-efficient method for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates fault-tolerant quantum computation using good quantum LDPC codes, achieving constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically suffers from high overhead in qubits and time. The authors aim to reduce both by leveraging quantum LDPC codes with constant rate and linear distance.
method: They propose a scheme that combines parallelized code surgery with locally testable state preparation, enabling efficient logical operations on LDPC codes.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving over previous approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can be used to accelerate fault-tolerant computation, offering a promising path toward practical quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating non-projective measurements by projective ones, with experimental validation on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are incomplete or not robust to noise. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete certification method.
method: They develop a new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy that can certify the impossibility of simulating a given measurement by projective measurements, and implement it experimentally on a trapped-ion system.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the experimental demonstration confirms the theoretical predictions, showing that non-projective measurements can be certified in practice.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, offering a complete and robust tool that is experimentally feasible, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for quantum technologies. The authors aim to model a quantum detector as an autonomous machine to assess its nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
method: They introduce a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, likely using fluctuation theorems or entropy production calculations to quantify the trade-off between measurement accuracy and thermodynamic cost.
result: The model demonstrates fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition, which is relevant for designing efficient quantum detectors and understanding the physical limits of measurement.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scaling quantum networks and computing requires controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which are challenging due to spectral diffusion and individual addressing.
method: The paper introduces a control framework that uses global driving and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging ensemble properties for scalability.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement generation with reduced experimental overhead, demonstrated for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable quantum information processing using solid-state spin ensembles, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, enhancing quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from resource inefficiency and complexity. The authors aim to improve repeater performance and practicality.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree codes and design optimized asymmetric code geometries, likely through numerical optimization or analytical modeling.
result: The joint approach boosts quantum repeater performance, reducing resource overhead and improving loss tolerance, making repeaters more feasible with current technology.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric code designs offer a resource-efficient path toward practical quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity as a technology.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical foundations of CV quantum communication, including Gaussian states and operations, and surveys experimental implementations and security proofs for CV-QKD and other protocols.
result: The review consolidates the state of the art in CV quantum communication, demonstrating its practical viability and theoretical robustness, and identifies future directions.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising field with significant potential for practical quantum networks, warranting continued research and development.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a unified overview of protocols and their security.
method: The authors review and classify various quantum cryptographic primitives, discussing their theoretical security guarantees and limitations, and survey current photonic implementations.
result: The review presents a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives, highlights the security and limitations of each, and summarizes experimental progress in photonic platforms.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich landscape of protocols beyond QKD, with practical implementations emerging, though many face significant theoretical and experimental challenges.

title: Quantum Kinetic Uncertainty Relations In Mesoscopic Conductors At Strong Coupling
authors: Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, And Géraldine Haack
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, and Géraldine Haack

Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) set fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport by bounding the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of the dynamical activity, a quantity that counts exchange events between a system and its reservoirs. This framework is well establishe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056302] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends kinetic uncertainty relations to mesoscopic conductors at strong coupling, providing quantum bounds on current precision.
motivation: Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) are fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport, but their validity at strong coupling is unclear. The authors aim to establish quantum KURs for mesoscopic conductors beyond weak coupling.
method: They derive quantum kinetic uncertainty relations for mesoscopic conductors using a full counting statistics approach, incorporating strong system-reservoir coupling and quantum coherence effects.
result: They obtain bounds on the signal-to-noise ratio of currents that depend on the dynamical activity and quantum corrections, showing that strong coupling can enhance or suppress precision depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for kinetic uncertainty relations in strongly coupled quantum transport, with implications for thermodynamic precision in nanoscale devices.

title: Experimental Realization Of Thermal Reservoirs With Tunable Temperature In A Trapped-Ion Spin-Boson Simulator
authors: Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, And Guido Pagano
abstract:
Author(s): Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, and Guido Pagano

We propose and demonstrate an experimental scheme to engineer thermal baths with independently tunable temperatures and dissipation rates for the motional modes of a trapped-ion system. This approach enables robust thermal-state preparation and quantum simulations of open-system dynamics in bosonic …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050604] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a trapped-ion simulator that realizes thermal reservoirs with independently tunable temperature and dissipation rates for bosonic modes, enabling quantum simulations of open-system dynamics.
motivation: The ability to engineer controllable thermal baths is crucial for studying open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics, but existing methods often lack independent control over temperature and dissipation.
method: The authors propose and implement a scheme using a trapped-ion system where the motional modes are coupled to engineered reservoirs, allowing independent tuning of temperature and dissipation rates via laser-induced interactions.
result: They demonstrate robust thermal-state preparation and simulate open-system dynamics, showing the tunability and control of the engineered thermal reservoirs.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile platform for quantum simulations of open-system dynamics and thermodynamic processes, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Non-Gaussianity From Superselection Rules
authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, And Pérola Milman
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, and Pérola Milman

Stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation to non-Gaussianity in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050203] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum systems, emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.
motivation: Non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum information processing with continuous variables, but its physical origin is not fully understood. The authors aim to provide a deeper interpretation by linking it to superselection rules and entanglement.
method: The paper uses theoretical analysis to connect stellar rank with superselection rules, likely employing group-theoretic and entanglement-theoretic tools to demonstrate that non-Gaussian states can be seen as possessing intrinsic multimode entanglement.
result: The authors establish that stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules, offering a new interpretation of non-Gaussianity as a manifestation of intrinsic multimode entanglement.
conclusion: This work provides a novel conceptual bridge between non-Gaussianity and entanglement, potentially impacting quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

Feedback control in open quantum dynamics is crucial for the advancement of various coherent platforms. However, currently only a handful of feedback master equations exist in the literature, which are restricted to specific types of feedback. In this letter we first introduce a unifying framework, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050401] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a unifying framework for feedback control in open quantum systems, deriving deterministic master equations for various feedback types.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for coherent platforms, but existing feedback master equations are limited to specific types, hindering broader applications.
method: The authors develop a general framework that unifies existing feedback master equations and derive deterministic equations for feedback control in open quantum systems.
result: The framework provides a systematic way to model feedback control, potentially enabling new applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of feedback control in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Game-theoretic Discovery Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes Through Nash Equilibria
authors: Rubén Darío Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Darío Guerrero

Quantum error-correction code discovery has relied on algebraic constructions with predetermined structure or computational search lacking equilibrium-topology analysis. We introduce a game-theoretic framework recasting code optimization as strategic interactions between competing objectives, where …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012465] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a game-theoretic approach to discover quantum error-correcting codes by framing code optimization as a Nash equilibrium between competing objectives.
motivation: Traditional algebraic constructions and computational searches for quantum error-correcting codes lack equilibrium-topology analysis, motivating a new framework that captures strategic trade-offs in code design.
method: The authors model code optimization as a game where competing objectives (e.g., error correction capability vs. resource overhead) are players, and use Nash equilibrium concepts to guide the search for optimal codes.
result: The framework yields new quantum error-correcting codes and provides insights into the equilibrium structure of code parameters, demonstrating the utility of game theory in code discovery.
conclusion: Game-theoretic optimization offers a novel and effective paradigm for discovering quantum error-correcting codes, potentially advancing quantum error correction.

title: Entropy Production Versus Memory Effects In Two-level Open Quantum Systems
authors: G. Théret, D. Sugny, And C. L. Latune
abstract:
Author(s): G. Théret, D. Sugny, and C. L. Latune

We compare several definitions of entropy production rate introduced in the literature from a large variety of situations and motivations, and then analyze their relations with memory effects. Considering a relevant experimental example of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode playing the r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012456] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares various entropy production rate definitions for a qubit interacting with a bosonic mode, analyzing their relation to memory effects.
motivation: To clarify the relationship between entropy production and non-Markovianity in open quantum systems, as different definitions may capture different aspects.
method: The authors analytically and numerically compare several entropy production rate formulas for a two-level system coupled to a single bosonic mode, examining their behavior in the presence of memory effects.
result: They find that different entropy production definitions can lead to different conclusions about the second law and memory effects, with some showing negative entropy production in non-Markovian regimes.
conclusion: The choice of entropy production definition is crucial for interpreting thermodynamic behavior in non-Markovian quantum systems, and memory effects can lead to apparent violations of the second law depending on the definition used.

title: Fault-tolerant non-Clifford Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Gates Using Polynomial Phase Gates And On-demand Noise Biasing
authors: Minh T. P. Nguyen And Mackenzie H. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T. P. Nguyen and Mackenzie H. Shaw

The Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) error correcting code uses a bosonic mode to encode a logical qubit and has the attractive property that its logical Clifford gates can be implemented using Gaussian unitary gates. In contrast, a direct unitary implementation of the [MATH] gate using the cubic phase …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033107] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford GKP gates using polynomial phase gates and on-demand noise biasing, advancing quantum error correction.
motivation: Direct unitary implementation of non-Clifford gates like the cubic phase gate in GKP codes is challenging; the authors aim to provide a fault-tolerant alternative.
method: They use polynomial phase gates combined with on-demand noise biasing to implement non-Clifford gates, analyzing the resulting error correction properties.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with improved noise resilience, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and simulations.
conclusion: The work offers a practical path for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with GKP codes, relevant to quantum error correction and information processing.

title: Achieving Phase-regulated Robust Quantum Entanglement In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, And Chun-Jie Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, and Chun-Jie Yang

Generating strongly entangled states within multiparticle systems stands as a pivotal endeavor in quantum physics. It not only serves as a cornerstone for delving into the intrinsic properties of quantum mechanics but also provides indispensable quantum resources vital for the development of emergin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033102] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust phase-regulated quantum entanglement in a cavity magnomechanical system, a hybrid quantum platform.
motivation: Generating strong entanglement in multiparticle systems is crucial for quantum technologies, and cavity magnomechanics offers a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a cavity magnomechanical system, showing how to achieve and regulate entanglement between magnons, photons, and phonons via phase control.
result: They find that robust entanglement can be generated and its strength and robustness can be tuned by adjusting the phase of the driving fields.
conclusion: The results provide a practical route to controllable entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, relevant for quantum information processing and networking.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: To enhance the performance of hybrid quantum systems by understanding and mitigating loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits.
method: The authors experimentally characterize and optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators, likely using fabrication and measurement techniques to assess phonon coherence and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence time and cooperativity, and identify materials strategies for reducing losses.
conclusion: The work provides a materials blueprint for advancing quantum acoustics and hybrid quantum systems, potentially enabling better quantum transducers and memories.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, exploiting high-spin nuclei to accumulate entanglement.
result: Demonstrates a universal approach for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, potentially enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical path toward higher-dimensional quantum communication using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during transmon readout limit readout fidelity, which is crucial for quantum error correction and scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors perform experiments on a transmon device with a cosφ coupling and compare with numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the nonlinear coupling.
result: They demonstrate that the cosφ coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The proposed nonlinear coupling offers a promising route to improve transmon readout, which is relevant for advancing superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank dictates the minimum resources required for preparing, compressing, and measuring bosonic quantum states, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a powerful tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating spectral instability in single-photon emitters is crucial for scalable quantum networks and quantum computation.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, using spectroscopic techniques to analyze spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into improving emitter coherence for quantum applications.
conclusion: The findings advance the development of stable single-photon sources for quantum networking, highlighting the potential of erbium in silicon as a promising platform.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies randomly monitored quantum codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and revealing new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and monitored dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, focusing on the decodability of the encoded information and the effect of measurement outcomes on logical error rates.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they characterize stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction, potentially informing the design of more efficient quantum error correction protocols.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical features of gravity.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity by proposing experiments that detect gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between quantum probes, which would demonstrate non-classicality of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (e.g., entanglement) and analyzes several proposed tabletop-scale GIE experiments, discussing their feasibility and implications.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for GIE, highlighting the potential to test quantum aspects of gravity in laboratory settings.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a promising path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a key focus for future tests.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates passive quantum error correction of photon loss at the breakeven point using continuous drives, extending a qubit's lifetime beyond its physical limits.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. The goal is to achieve error correction passively, using engineered dissipation or continuous drives, to protect quantum information more efficiently.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives on a superconducting circuit, likely a cavity or transmon system, to correct for photon loss errors without active measurement or feedback.
result: They achieve error correction at the breakeven point, meaning the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the uncorrected physical lifetime, demonstrating a net benefit from the passive scheme.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction can be effective at breakeven, offering a simpler alternative to active schemes and potentially improving qubit coherence in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum processors.
method: Designs twisted color circuits that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, and uses a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates a scalable circuit family that achieves fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates, potentially reducing overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: Provides a promising path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures, with implications for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones, especially in linear algebra tasks.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, showing where quantum advantage may be possible.
conclusion: The findings contribute to quantum computational complexity theory, potentially guiding future algorithm development.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential practical applications.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer exponential speedups for this task.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and amplitude estimation to compute persistence diagrams, achieving exponential speedup over classical methods under certain conditions.
result: The algorithm provides provable quantum speedups for computing persistence in TDA, with rigorous complexity analysis showing exponential improvement in relevant parameters.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a concrete quantum advantage for a practical data analysis problem, potentially motivating further research and applications in quantum machine learning and data science.

title: Alternative Upper Bound For Accessible Information And Wave-particle Duality
authors: Weizhe Gao And Sixia Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Gao and Sixia Yu

Accessible information of an ensemble, together with its Holevo bound, plays an essential role in quantum information science. Here, we report an alternative upper bound for accessible information based on a relation between accessible information and entanglement. Our bound can tighten the Holevo b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012466] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an alternative upper bound for accessible information that can tighten the Holevo bound, based on a relation between accessible information and entanglement.
motivation: Accessible information is a fundamental quantity in quantum information, and the Holevo bound is a well-known upper bound. Finding tighter bounds is important for understanding the limits of information transmission.
method: The authors derive a new upper bound for accessible information using a relation between accessible information and entanglement, likely involving entanglement measures or monogamy.
result: The proposed bound can be tighter than the Holevo bound in certain cases, providing a more precise characterization of accessible information.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum information theory by offering a new tool for bounding accessible information, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Enhancing Long-distance Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With An Error-correcting Relay
authors: S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, And Timothy C. Ralph
abstract:
Author(s): S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, and Timothy C. Ralph

Noiseless linear amplifiers serve as an effective means to enable long-distance continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD), even under realistic conditions with nonunit reconciliation efficiency. Separately, unitary averaging has been suggested to mitigate some stochastic noise, includi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012625] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an error-correcting relay based on noiseless linear amplification and unitary averaging to enhance the performance of long-distance continuous-variable quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD suffers from distance limitations due to noise and loss. Noiseless linear amplifiers can help, but their performance is limited by nonunit reconciliation efficiency and stochastic noise.
method: The authors combine noiseless linear amplification with unitary averaging to mitigate stochastic noise, and introduce an error-correcting relay that uses these techniques to improve the signal quality for long-distance CV-QKD.
result: The proposed relay significantly extends the achievable distance and improves the secret key rate of CV-QKD under realistic conditions, including nonunit reconciliation efficiency.
conclusion: The error-correcting relay offers a practical and effective solution for long-distance CV-QKD, potentially enabling secure communication over extended distances.

title: Full Schmidt Characterization Of Spatiotemporally Entangled States Produced From Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Rakesh Pradhan And Girish Kulkarni
abstract:
Author(s): Rakesh Pradhan and Girish Kulkarni

The full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states generated from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) has not been carried out until now due to the immense computational complexity arising from the large dimensionalities of the states. In this article, we utilize the rotat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013722] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents the first full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states from SPDC using a rotation-based method, providing a complete characterization of their entanglement structure.
motivation: The full Schmidt decomposition of SPDC states has been computationally intractable due to high dimensionality, limiting understanding of their entanglement properties. The authors aim to overcome this challenge to enable precise characterization.
method: They employ a rotation-based approach to compute the Schmidt decomposition of the spatiotemporal biphoton state, handling the large Hilbert space efficiently.
result: They obtain the full Schmidt decomposition, revealing the entanglement spectrum and mode structure of the SPDC state, and analyze its dependence on experimental parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a complete tool for characterizing spatiotemporal entanglement in SPDC, with implications for quantum information processing and quantum communication.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between experimental demonstrations and theoretical hardness results.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime. The authors aim to provide rigorous foundations for the saturated regime.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling with a linear number of modes, likely using techniques from computational complexity theory and quantum information, such as worst-case to average-case reductions and anticoncentration properties.
result: They prove hardness results for BosonSampling in the saturated regime, showing that approximate sampling is classically hard under plausible complexity assumptions.
conclusion: The work validates the quantum advantage of photonic experiments in the saturated regime, providing theoretical support for current and future demonstrations.
