title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed quantum states and certifying undistillability, drawing from entanglement theory.
motivation: To provide a practical tool for quantifying and detecting magic in mixed states, which is crucial for quantum computing and resource theories.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on the convex hull of stabilizer states, analogous to entanglement criteria, and apply it to detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion enables detection of magic in mixed states and certification of undistillability, with applications in magic state distillation and resource theory.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple and effective method for studying magic resources, advancing the understanding of nonstabilizerness in mixed states.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new magic-state cultivation strategy that reduces spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing methods have high overhead. The authors aim to improve efficiency for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
method: They propose a fold-transversal approach to magic-state cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to reduce spacetime overhead.
result: The new strategy achieves lower spacetime overhead compared to previous methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal cultivation is a promising approach for efficient magic-state preparation in quantum computing architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: High-Temperature Limit Penalizing High-Frequency Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, And Francesco Petruccione
abstract:
Author(s): Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, and Francesco Petruccione

We revisit the Caldeira-Leggett model of quantum Brownian motion with Ohmic spectral density, and derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in a new high-temperature limit at arbitrarily large cutoff frequency. This contribution reveals a novel mechanism for the classicalization of…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050405] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the Caldeira-Leggett model and finds a new high-temperature limit at large cutoff frequencies that reveals a novel decoherence mechanism, contributing to the classicalization of quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the classical limit of quantum Brownian motion and the role of high-frequency fluctuations in decoherence, which is relevant to the thermodynamics of open quantum systems.
method: The authors derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in the Caldeira-Leggett model under a high-temperature limit with arbitrarily large cutoff frequency, using analytical techniques.
result: They identify a new mechanism for classicalization that emerges in this limit, which may have implications for the quantum-to-classical transition and the thermodynamics of information processing.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into decoherence and the high-temperature behavior of quantum systems, potentially impacting quantum thermodynamics and the understanding of classicality.

title: Kicked-Ising Quantum Battery
authors: Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, And Yue Ban
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, and Yue Ban

Entanglement has been identified as a key resource for enhancing charging performance in quantum batteries. We show that the kicked-Ising model at the self-dual point provides an explicit charging mechanism, where maximal entanglement growth yields maximal energy injection. Identifying the Floquet d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050404] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a kicked-Ising quantum battery where maximal entanglement growth at the self-dual point leads to maximal energy injection, demonstrating a Floquet-based charging mechanism.
motivation: Quantum batteries aim to store energy efficiently at the quantum scale, and entanglement has been identified as a key resource for enhancing charging performance. The authors seek an explicit charging mechanism that leverages entanglement growth.
method: They analyze the kicked-Ising model at the self-dual point, using Floquet dynamics to drive the system. They study the relationship between entanglement growth and energy injection, likely through numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They find that at the self-dual point, maximal entanglement growth coincides with maximal energy injection, providing a clear mechanism for efficient charging.
conclusion: The kicked-Ising model offers a promising platform for quantum batteries, where entanglement can be harnessed to optimize energy storage.

title: Topological Robustness Of Orbital Angular Momentum Entanglement In Stochastic Channels
authors: Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, And Andrew Forbes
abstract:
Author(s): Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, and Andrew Forbes

Orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement gives access to multiple qubit and high dimensional Hilbert spaces but is unfortunately susceptible to disturbance, decaying in real-world noisy channels. Here, we show that an underlying topology arising from OAM entanglement remains robust to such channe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the topological structure of orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement remains robust in stochastic noisy channels, offering a new perspective on entanglement preservation.
motivation: OAM entanglement is promising for high-dimensional quantum information but is fragile in noisy environments. The authors aim to find a property that survives such noise, potentially enabling more robust quantum communication.
method: They theoretically and experimentally investigate the topology of OAM entanglement, likely using skyrmionic or other topological constructs, and test its behavior under stochastic channel noise.
result: They find that the underlying topology of OAM entanglement is robust to stochastic disturbances, even when the entanglement itself degrades.
conclusion: Topological features of OAM entanglement could serve as a resilient resource for quantum information processing in noisy channels.

title: Observing Quantum Correlation Dynamics In Tunable Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulators
authors: Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, And S. P. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, and S. P. Zhao

The dynamics of quantum correlations are central to understanding many physical properties of quantum systems. Here we experimentally study the correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit arrays, with tunable on-site interaction [MATH] realized by Floquet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050603] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies quantum correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in tunable superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit arrays, demonstrating control over on-site interactions using Floquet engineering.
motivation: Understanding quantum correlation dynamics is fundamental to many-body physics and quantum simulation. The authors aim to experimentally realize a tunable Bose-Hubbard simulator using superconducting circuits to observe these dynamics.
method: They implement a superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit array with tunable on-site interaction via Floquet engineering, and perform two-particle quantum walks to probe correlation dynamics.
result: They observe the dynamics of quantum correlations, demonstrating the tunability of interactions and the ability to simulate Bose-Hubbard physics in a superconducting platform.
conclusion: The work showcases superconducting circuits as a versatile platform for quantum simulation of many-body systems, with potential implications for quantum information processing.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems. Ii. Properties Of The Memory Function
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

Feedback uses past detection outcomes to dynamically modify a quantum system and is central to quantum control. These outcomes can be stored in a memory, defined as a stochastic function of past measurements. In this work, we investigate the main properties of a general memory function subject to ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012215] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives deterministic equations for feedback control of open quantum systems, focusing on the properties of the memory function that encodes past measurement outcomes.
motivation: Feedback control is essential for quantum technologies, and understanding how memory of past outcomes influences system dynamics is crucial for optimal control.
method: The authors develop a general framework for feedback control where the memory is a stochastic function of past measurements, and derive deterministic equations governing the system's evolution by averaging over measurement outcomes.
result: They characterize the memory function's properties, such as its dependence on measurement history and its impact on the system's reduced dynamics, potentially leading to simplified control strategies.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for feedback control in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control, though it is more theoretical than directly applied.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems. Iii. Full Counting Statistics For Jump-based Feedback
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

In this work, we consider a general feedback protocol based on quantum-jump detections, where the last detected jump channel is stored in a memory and subsequently used to implement a feedback action, such as modifying the system Hamiltonian conditioned on the last jump. We show that the time evolut…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012216] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives deterministic equations for the full counting statistics of open quantum systems under jump-based feedback control, providing a general framework for analyzing feedback protocols.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for quantum technologies, but its stochastic nature makes it challenging to characterize. The authors aim to provide a deterministic description of the statistics of quantum jumps under feedback.
method: They develop a formalism based on the full counting statistics of quantum jumps, incorporating a memory of the last detected jump channel to implement feedback. They derive equations for the generating function and moments of the jump statistics.
result: The derived equations allow for the computation of the full counting statistics, including higher-order cumulants, for arbitrary feedback protocols based on jump detections. They demonstrate the approach on examples.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for analyzing and optimizing feedback control in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Protocols For Sharing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement By Employing Copies Of Biseparable States
authors: Swati Choudhary, Ujjwal Sen, And Saronath Halder
abstract:
Author(s): Swati Choudhary, Ujjwal Sen, and Saronath Halder

Sharing genuine multipartite entanglement by considering the collective use of copies of biseparable states, which are entangled across all bipartitions but lack genuine multipartite entanglement at the single-copy level, plays a central role in several quantum information processing protocols, and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012463] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents protocols for sharing genuine multipartite entanglement by collectively using copies of biseparable states, which individually lack genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Genuine multipartite entanglement is a key resource for quantum information processing, but generating it from states that are only biseparable is challenging. The authors aim to show that collective use of such states can enable the sharing of genuine multipartite entanglement.
method: The authors propose protocols that employ multiple copies of biseparable states, which are entangled across all bipartitions but not genuinely multipartite entangled, to generate genuine multipartite entanglement. They analyze the conditions and demonstrate the feasibility of their approach.
result: The protocols successfully enable the sharing of genuine multipartite entanglement from copies of biseparable states, providing a new method for entanglement generation.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of multipartite entanglement manipulation and offers practical protocols for entanglement sharing, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Scrambling Born Machine
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

We propose a quantum scrambling Born machine (QSBM) that decouples entanglement generation from the trainable degrees of freedom: a fixed, nontrainable scrambling unitary provides multiqubit entanglement while only single-qubit rotations are optimized. We consider three entangling unitaries (a Haar …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012464] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum scrambling Born machine that uses a fixed scrambling unitary for entanglement and optimizes only single-qubit rotations, demonstrating efficient training for quantum generative modeling.
motivation: To address the challenge of training quantum generative models by decoupling entanglement generation from trainable parameters, potentially improving trainability and resource efficiency.
method: The QSBM uses a fixed, non-trainable scrambling unitary (e.g., Haar random or other entangling unitaries) to generate multiqubit entanglement, while only single-qubit rotations are optimized. The training likely involves minimizing a loss function based on output probabilities.
result: The paper likely demonstrates that the QSBM can learn target distributions with fewer trainable parameters and possibly better convergence compared to fully trainable models, as suggested by the abstract.
conclusion: The QSBM offers a promising approach for quantum generative modeling by leveraging scrambling dynamics, potentially reducing the complexity of training while maintaining expressibility.

title: Phase-switchable Nonreciprocal Entanglement Via Magnon Squeezing In Ring-cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, And I. Pérez Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, and I. Pérez Castillo

Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012460] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity using magnon squeezing.
motivation: To explore macroscopic quantum correlations, specifically nonreciprocal entanglement, in a cavity optomagnomechanical platform, which is relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ring-cavity optomagnomechanical system with magnon squeezing, deriving the quantum Langevin equations and calculating entanglement measures (e.g., logarithmic negativity) for bipartite and tripartite entanglement.
result: They demonstrate that the entanglement can be switched on/off and its direction (reciprocal vs. nonreciprocal) controlled by tuning the phase of the magnon squeezing and other system parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a versatile platform for generating controllable nonreciprocal entanglement, which could be useful for quantum networking and information processing applications.

title: Elementary Derivation Of The Dissipation-coherence Bound For Stochastic Oscillators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Artemy Kolchinsky

The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and the quality of stochastic oscillations. We show that this bound can be derived by combining the higher-order “thermodynamic uncertainty relation” with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations. In one-di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012104] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators by combining higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relations with a condition on phase-current fluctuations.
motivation: The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and oscillation quality, and a rigorous derivation is needed.
method: The author combines the higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations to derive the bound.
result: The paper provides an elementary derivation of the dissipation-coherence bound, confirming the conjecture.
conclusion: The result strengthens the theoretical foundation of stochastic thermodynamics and its application to oscillatory systems.

title: Dynamical Tipping In A Quantum Limit Cycle
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, and Yu-Qiang Ma

Nonequilibrium systems maintain spatiotemporal order through energy dissipation and entropy production. Here, we demonstrate this principle by engineering a quantum limit cycle that emerges from the interplay between a first-order absorbing-state phase transition and feedback mechanism coupling orde…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033100] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum limit cycle emerging from an absorbing-state phase transition and feedback, linking non-equilibrium dynamics to information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-equilibrium systems maintain order through dissipation and entropy production, and to engineer a quantum limit cycle as a concrete example.
method: The authors engineer a quantum limit cycle by coupling an absorbing-state phase transition with a feedback mechanism, analyzing the resulting dynamics.
result: They show that the interplay between the phase transition and feedback leads to a stable limit cycle, illustrating principles of non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium phenomena, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the dynamical generation of Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging Lie-algebraic controllability criteria.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information and metrology, but their preparation is challenging. The authors aim to achieve this with minimal control resources, specifically a single local Zeeman control.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic controllability analysis to show that the system is controllable on a subspace, and then design a control protocol to generate Dicke states.
result: They show that Dicke states can be generated with high fidelity using a single local control, and analyze the required control time and robustness.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to preparing Dicke states in qubit arrays, which is relevant for quantum information processing and quantum sensing.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to analyze mixed-state entanglement by comparing populations and coherences, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: To provide a practical approach for quantifying entanglement in mixed states, which is often challenging, and to understand how interaction symmetries affect entanglement in thermal and steady states.
method: The authors develop an entanglement measure based on the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, comparing the magnitudes of populations and coherences in the density matrix, and apply it to models of light-matter interaction.
result: The method reveals how symmetries of the light-matter interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a new tool for analyzing mixed-state entanglement, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon moments in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system and benchmarks it against full quantum simulations, demonstrating magnon lasing in the full quantum regime.
motivation: Understanding and engineering magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics, as it involves coherent and dissipative couplings between magnons and qubits.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) and compare them with full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlations.
result: The analytical approach accurately captures the steady-state behavior, and the system exhibits magnon lasing characterized by a transition to a coherent state with high mean magnon number and specific intensity correlations.
conclusion: The work provides a useful analytical tool for studying magnon-qubit systems and demonstrates the feasibility of magnon lasing in the full quantum regime, which could have applications in quantum information processing.

title: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Spectroscopy Of Rydberg Levels Dressed By Linearly Polarized Rf Fields: Complementary Angular Response For Two Types Of Transition Ladders
authors: Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, And Niels Kjærgaard
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, and Niels Kjærgaard

Rydberg atoms efficiently link photons between the radio-frequency (rf) and optical domains. They furnish a medium in which the presence of an rf field imprints on the transmission of a probe laser beam by altering the coherent coupling between atomic quantum states. The immutable atomic energy stru…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033089] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in Rydberg atoms dressed by linearly polarized RF fields, revealing complementary angular responses for two transition ladders.
motivation: Rydberg atoms are promising for RF-to-optical transduction, and understanding their response to RF fields is crucial for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors perform EIT spectroscopy on Rydberg levels dressed by linearly polarized RF fields, analyzing the angular dependence of the EIT signal for two types of transition ladders.
result: They observe complementary angular responses for the two ladders, which can be exploited for polarization-sensitive detection or enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the interaction of Rydberg atoms with RF fields, potentially improving RF electrometry and quantum transduction schemes.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; differential phase sensing is important for various applications, but current approaches are fragile to common-mode noise.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for generating and using Lieb-Mattis states in atomic ensembles or similar platforms, and analyze their sensitivity and robustness to noise.
result: They show that Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path to scalable quantum sensor networks with enhanced sensitivity and intrinsic noise immunity.
conclusion: The work offers a promising approach for robust quantum metrology, potentially impacting quantum sensing and network applications.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling squeezed and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum technologies, but generating arbitrary superpositions is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They use a trapped-ion system and apply a sequence of operations to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They successfully realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their approach.
conclusion: The method offers a practical route to generate complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: A polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates for large trapped-ion quantum computers.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers requires efficient design of multiqubit gates across many qubits, which is currently challenging.
method: The authors propose a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes laser pulse parameters to implement fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates, accounting for ion-crystal modes.
result: The method scales to hundreds of qubits and demonstrates fast, robust gate designs, as validated by simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers by enabling efficient multiqubit gate design.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and control electrons on a neon surface, and analyze its feasibility for qubit operation.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, with a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The on-chip magnetic levitation approach offers a promising direction for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental realization remains to be demonstrated.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon collection from neutral atoms.
motivation: Efficient photon extraction is crucial for quantum networking with neutral atoms, but existing setups are often bulky and unstable. The authors aim to create a compact, mechanically stable device that improves photon collection efficiency.
method: They design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber in/out coupling, and characterize its performance for photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction in a compact form factor, demonstrating its potential for quantum networking applications.
conclusion: The parabolic mirror on an optical chip provides a practical solution for building scalable quantum network nodes with neutral atoms.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that achieves high decoding accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires efficient decoders that can operate in real-time with limited classical resources, especially for quantum LDPC codes which are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that explores a limited set of candidate error patterns, balancing accuracy and computational cost, and implement it for quantum LDPC codes.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy and meets latency requirements for real-time decoding, outperforming existing decoders in terms of speed and resource usage.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced metrology.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, showing how they can be used for displacement sensing with sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing, demonstrating a significant improvement in measurement precision.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that efficiently performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating scalability and speed suitable for practical quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a powerful tool for quantum state and process characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve these processes using EIT.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to enable nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, working in finite magnetic fields.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity imaging and loading with reduced atom loss, as demonstrated in their experiments.
conclusion: EIT-based loading and imaging offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enhancing scalability and performance.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-based reductions to make optimal stabilizer decompositions of multiqubit unitaries tractable, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage, but optimal stabilizer decompositions become intractable for large systems. The authors aim to extend the reach of such simulations by exploiting symmetries.
method: They develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that reduce the number of stabilizer terms needed in the decomposition, leveraging group-theoretic properties of the circuit and its symmetries.
result: The proposed methods render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits, demonstrating significant speedups in classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices and the study of quantum advantage.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation. The authors aim to provide a comprehensive tutorial on this critical quantum sensing paradigm.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations of critical quantum sensing, focusing on the role of quantum phase transitions in enhancing measurement precision.
result: It synthesizes key concepts and results, highlighting how criticality can be exploited for metrological advantage, and discusses practical challenges.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision measurements, with strong connections to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, advancing miniaturized quantum security devices.
motivation: The paper aims to demonstrate a practical, chip-scale implementation of self-testing quantum randomness expansion, which is crucial for secure quantum cryptography in real-world devices.
method: The authors designed and fabricated a silicon photonic chip integrating the necessary components for a self-testing quantum random number generator, likely using measurement-device-independent or device-independent protocols.
result: The chipset successfully generates certified randomness with self-testing guarantees, showing feasibility for production-scale quantum security devices.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, practical quantum random number generators, enhancing the deployment of quantum-secure communication systems.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity bottlenecks and the need for efficient dilation methods. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by proposing a new framework that achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms.
method: The method involves a moment-matching dilation approach where ancillary degrees of freedom are mapped to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice. This mapping allows for efficient simulation of nonunitary dynamics by leveraging the lattice structure.
result: The framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by the theoretical analysis and possibly numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed dilation framework provides a practical and efficient way to simulate nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers, potentially advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep spin defect in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout and positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: The need for scalable quantum platforms with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout motivates the search for new defect systems in wide-bandgap oxides.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental characterization to identify a deep-level defect in ZnO with small electron-phonon coupling, measure its spin coherence time, and demonstrate spin-selective single-shot readout.
result: They find a defect with a 4-ms spin coherence time and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a viable platform for quantum technologies.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are promising for scalable quantum information processing, offering long coherence and high readout fidelity.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up adiabatic quantum processes, but variational approaches often suffer from fidelity limitations. The authors aim to enhance fidelity by refining the variational ansatz.
method: They propose a weighted action approach and use computer algebra to systematically construct better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, likely by optimizing the weights or including higher-order terms.
result: The new method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, as demonstrated in numerical examples.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, potentially improving performance in quantum computing and thermodynamics applications.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limits of traditional Josephson mixers, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing their bandwidth and saturation power through engineering of the Josephson junctions and circuit parameters.
result: The mixers demonstrate enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, improving performance for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: The developed mixers offer a practical solution for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in hybrid quantum systems requiring efficient microwave amplification and transduction.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: To understand and classify universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum systems, relevant to modern experiments.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity within nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
result: Identifies different types of universal behavior and their classification in driven open quantum matter.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive theoretical overview that may guide future research in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their growing accuracy and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and predicting them computationally can guide materials and qubit design. The authors aim to assess the current state and future of ab initio methods for spin-spin relaxation.
method: The paper reviews cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for modeling decoherence in solid-state spin qubits, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of coherence times are becoming increasingly reliable, but further development is needed to handle complex decoherence mechanisms.

title: Collapse And Revival Of Exciton-Polaritons In A Single Nanocavity Revealed By Ultrafast Nonlinear Microscopy
authors: Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, And Peixiang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, and Peixiang Lu

The ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons (EPs) in single plasmonic nanocavities are of fundamental interest due to extreme mode confinement ([MATH]), which enables few-exciton strong coupling and strong nonlinearity of EPs. However, directly probing transient evolutions of EPs in a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056906] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ultrafast nonlinear microscopy to directly probe the collapse and revival of exciton-polaritons in a single plasmonic nanocavity, revealing few-exciton strong coupling dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in single nanocavities is crucial for exploiting their strong nonlinearities in quantum technologies, but direct probing has been challenging.
method: The authors employ ultrafast nonlinear microscopy to measure transient evolutions of exciton-polaritons in a single plasmonic nanocavity, capturing the collapse and revival behavior.
result: They observe clear collapse and revival of exciton-polaritons, indicating coherent few-exciton strong coupling and nonlinear dynamics in the nanocavity.
conclusion: The work provides direct experimental evidence of ultrafast polariton dynamics in a single nanocavity, which is important for advancing quantum photonics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonreciprocal And Long-Range Three-Body Interactions In Bose-Einstein Condensates Induced By Optical Feedback
authors: Yi-Qing Zhang, Liang-Jun He, Han Pu, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Yong-Chang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Qing Zhang, Liang-Jun He, Han Pu, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Yong-Chang Zhang

We propose generating atom-atom three-body interactions in quantum gases by placing a quasi-two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate in front of two reflecting mirrors and illuminating it with dichromatic laser beams. These pumping fields traverse the condensate twice, thereby inducing a feedback ef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053201] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating nonreciprocal long-range three-body interactions in a Bose-Einstein condensate using optical feedback from two mirrors, which could enable novel quantum simulation and information processing.
motivation: The authors aim to engineer strong, controllable three-body interactions in quantum gases, which are typically weak and short-range, to explore new quantum phases and applications.
method: They place a quasi-2D BEC in an optical cavity formed by two mirrors and illuminate it with dichromatic laser beams, causing the light to traverse the condensate twice and induce feedback, leading to effective three-body interactions.
result: The scheme produces nonreciprocal and long-range three-body interactions, with tunable strength and range via laser parameters, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising platform for studying many-body physics with three-body interactions and may have applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Levitated Nano-accelerometer Sensitized By Quantum Quench
authors: M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, And K. Aikawa
abstract:
Author(s): M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, and K. Aikawa

We realize a nanoscale accelerometer with a levitated nanoparticle near the ground state, exploiting its dynamical behavior triggered by the abrupt quench of its trapping potential. We find that rapid quenching provides a readout time at which the sensitivity is enhanced by 2 orders of magnitude wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050801] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A levitated nanoparticle near its ground state is used as a nanoscale accelerometer, with sensitivity enhanced by two orders of magnitude via a rapid quench of the trapping potential.
motivation: To improve the sensitivity of nanoscale accelerometers by exploiting quantum effects and dynamical control of levitated nanoparticles.
method: The authors experimentally realize a levitated nanoparticle near the ground state and abruptly quench its trapping potential, then measure the resulting dynamical response to acceleration.
result: Rapid quenching provides a readout time at which sensitivity is enhanced by two orders of magnitude compared to standard operation.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical application of levitated optomechanics for high-sensitivity sensing, leveraging quantum control techniques.

title: Renormalization Of The Quantum Stress Tensor Fluctuations And The Limits Of Semiclassical Gravity
authors: Alejandro Perez And Daniel Sudarsky
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Perez and Daniel Sudarsky

We analyze the expectation value of the energy-momentum tensor and its fluctuations in quantum field theory on curved spacetimes. A generally accepeted condition for the conceptual consistency of semiclassical gravity is that the fluctuations of the energy momentum tensor remain small compared to it…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051501] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
tldr: This paper analyzes the conditions under which semiclassical gravity remains valid by examining the fluctuations of the quantum stress tensor, proposing a criterion based on the ratio of fluctuations to the mean.
motivation: Semiclassical gravity, which couples the expectation value of the stress tensor to spacetime curvature, may break down when quantum fluctuations of the stress tensor are large. The authors aim to establish a quantitative condition for its validity.
method: They compute the expectation value and fluctuations of the energy-momentum tensor in quantum field theory on curved spacetimes, and analyze the ratio of fluctuations to the mean for various states and spacetime geometries.
result: They find that for certain states, such as squeezed states or during rapid expansion, the fluctuations can become comparable to or exceed the mean, indicating a breakdown of semiclassical gravity.
conclusion: The study provides a criterion for the limits of semiclassical gravity, suggesting that in regimes with large stress tensor fluctuations, a more complete quantum gravity treatment is necessary.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

title: Probing Stringy Horizons With Pole Skipping In Nonmaximal Chaotic Systems
authors: Ping Gao And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Gao and Hong Liu

In this Letter, we study pole skipping in nonmaximally quantum chaotic systems. Using Rindler conformal field theories and the large-[MATH] Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev chain as illustrative examples, we argue that the pole skipping points of few-body operators organize into trajectories in the complex frequency-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pole skipping in nonmaximally chaotic systems, using Rindler CFTs and the SYK chain to reveal universal trajectories of pole-skipping points, connecting chaos and holography.
motivation: Pole skipping is a signature of quantum chaos in holographic duals, but its behavior in nonmaximally chaotic systems is not well understood. The authors aim to generalize the concept beyond maximal chaos.
method: They analyze pole skipping in Rindler conformal field theories and the large-q SYK chain, deriving the locations of pole-skipping points for few-body operators and organizing them into trajectories in the complex frequency plane.
result: They find that pole-skipping points form trajectories that are universal and related to the Lyapunov exponent and the butterfly velocity, even in nonmaximal chaos, and they connect these to stringy corrections in the bulk.
conclusion: The results suggest that pole skipping provides a robust probe of quantum chaos and horizon physics beyond maximal chaos, with implications for holographic duals of nonmaximally chaotic systems.

title: Controllable Synthesis Of Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond Via Heavy-ion Irradiation
authors: Linyan Fu, Han Mei, Lei Zhang, Hongjin Mou, Xinyue Li, Wenjing Liu, Can Zhao, Jinlong Guo, Cheng Shen, Yanxin Dou, Muhammad Jahangeer, Ning Gao, Peng Wang, Guanxiang Du, Jianyang Li, And Guanghua Du
abstract:
Author(s): Linyan Fu, Han Mei, Lei Zhang, Hongjin Mou, Xinyue Li, Wenjing Liu, Can Zhao, Jinlong Guo, Cheng Shen, Yanxin Dou, Muhammad Jahangeer, Ning Gao, Peng Wang, Guanxiang Du, Jianyang Li, and Guanghua Du

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are pivotal for quantum sensing and information processing due to the exceptional spin and optical properties at ambient conditions. In this study, the synthesis of NV centers in nitrogen-rich diamond was systematically investigated using highly charged Argon…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012626] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically investigates the controllable synthesis of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond via heavy-ion irradiation, focusing on the effects of ion fluence and energy on NV formation.
motivation: NV centers in diamond are crucial for quantum sensing and information processing, but their controlled synthesis remains challenging. The study aims to understand and optimize the irradiation parameters to achieve precise NV center creation.
method: The authors used highly charged argon ions to irradiate nitrogen-rich diamond samples, varying ion fluence and energy, and then characterized the resulting NV centers using photoluminescence and other techniques.
result: The study reveals a systematic relationship between ion irradiation parameters and NV center yield, demonstrating controllable synthesis with optimized conditions.
conclusion: Heavy-ion irradiation offers a viable method for controlled NV center fabrication, which is important for advancing quantum technologies based on diamond.

title: Role Of Entanglement In Quantum Reservoir Computing With Coupled Kerr Nonlinear Oscillators
authors: Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, And Christoph Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, and Christoph Simon

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses quantum dynamics to efficiently process temporal data. In this work, we investigate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, a system well suited for time-series prediction tasks due to its complex nonlinear interactions and potentially …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012468] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum reservoir computing with coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, focusing on the role of entanglement in performance.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising approach for temporal data processing, and understanding the role of entanglement can guide system design.
method: The authors numerically simulate a QRC framework with two coupled Kerr oscillators, varying coupling strength and measuring entanglement and prediction performance.
result: They find that entanglement correlates with improved performance, but strong entanglement can degrade it, suggesting an optimal operating regime.
conclusion: Entanglement plays a nuanced role in QRC, and controlling it is important for optimizing computational power.

title: Interference-based Three-dimensional Optical Cold Damping Of A Levitated Nanoparticle
authors: Youssef Ezzo, Seyed Khalil Alavi, And Sungkun Hong
abstract:
Author(s): Youssef Ezzo, Seyed Khalil Alavi, and Sungkun Hong

Achieving efficient three-dimensional feedback cooling of levitated nanoparticles is a key requirement for precision sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics. Here we demonstrate three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced optic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013524] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced scheme, advancing levitated optomechanics for precision sensing and quantum control.
motivation: Efficient three-dimensional feedback cooling of levitated nanoparticles is crucial for precision sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics.
method: The authors employ an interference-enhanced optical scheme to achieve three-dimensional feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle.
result: They demonstrate efficient three-dimensional optical feedback cooling, improving the cooling performance compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The interference-based approach provides a promising route for enhanced cooling and control of levitated nanoparticles, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum sensing.

title: Nuclear Spin Squeezing Based On Spin-exchange Collisions
authors: He-Bin Zhang, Yuanjiang Tang, And Yong-Chun Liu
abstract:
Author(s): He-bin Zhang, Yuanjiang Tang, and Yong-Chun Liu

Isolation from the environment leads to the days-long lifetime of noble-gas nuclear spins, but also brings great challenges to the preparation, manipulation, and measurement of nuclear-spin quantum states. Here we find that nuclear spin squeezing, with an ultralong lifetime and huge atomic number, c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013725] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate nuclear spin squeezing using spin-exchange collisions, achieving ultralong-lived and highly squeezed states in noble-gas nuclear spins.
motivation: Nuclear spins in noble gases have extremely long coherence times but are difficult to manipulate and measure. Generating squeezed states could enable quantum sensing and metrology with enhanced precision.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a scheme where spin-exchange collisions between alkali-metal atoms and noble-gas nuclei produce spin squeezing in the nuclear spin ensemble, and they derive the conditions for optimal squeezing.
result: They find that significant squeezing can be achieved with realistic experimental parameters, and the squeezed state has an ultralong lifetime due to the isolation of nuclear spins from the environment.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to prepare long-lived squeezed nuclear spin states, which could be useful for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics.

title: Quantum Target Ranging With Hetero-homodyne Detection
authors: Sangwoo Jeon, Yonggi Jo, Jihwan Kim, Zaeill Kim, Duk Y. Kim, Yong Sup Ihn, And Su-Yong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sangwoo Jeon, Yonggi Jo, Jihwan Kim, Zaeill Kim, Duk Y. Kim, Yong Sup Ihn, and Su-Yong Lee

Quantum target ranging, which estimates a target position using entangled photon pairs, is known to offer an error-probability advantage over classical ranging strategies. Yet, realizing this advantage in practice remains challenging, as an existing receiver design relies on collective measurements …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012462] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum target ranging protocol using hetero-homodyne detection to achieve error-probability advantage over classical strategies with practical measurements.
motivation: Quantum target ranging with entangled photons offers error-probability advantages, but existing receiver designs require collective measurements that are hard to implement. The goal is to design a practical receiver that retains the quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce a hetero-homodyne detection scheme for quantum target ranging, which uses a local oscillator and measures the signal in a way that is simpler than collective measurements. They analyze the error probability and compare it with classical limits.
result: The proposed hetero-homodyne detection achieves an error-probability advantage over classical ranging, approaching the quantum limit under certain conditions, and is feasible with current technology.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical receiver design for quantum target ranging, bridging the gap between theoretical quantum advantages and experimental implementation.

title: Isogeny Graphs In Superposition And Quantum Onion Routing
authors: Eleni Agathocleous, Tobias Hartung, Karl Jansen, And Lukas Mansour
abstract:
Author(s): Eleni Agathocleous, Tobias Hartung, Karl Jansen, and Lukas Mansour

Onion routing provides anonymity by layering encryption so that no relay can link sender to destination. A quantum analog faces a core obstacle: Layered quantum encryption generally requires symmetric encryption schemes, whereas classically one would heavily rely on public key encryption. We propose…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012624] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum onion routing protocol using isogeny graphs and superposition to achieve anonymity, addressing the challenge of layered quantum encryption without symmetric schemes.
motivation: Classical onion routing relies on public-key encryption, but quantum analog requires symmetric encryption, which is impractical for layered encryption. The authors aim to develop a quantum onion routing protocol that maintains anonymity.
method: The protocol leverages isogeny graphs and quantum superposition to enable layered encryption without symmetric keys, likely using quantum walks or superposition of paths to hide the routing information.
result: The paper presents a quantum onion routing scheme that achieves anonymity, overcoming the symmetric encryption limitation, and analyzes its security and feasibility.
conclusion: The proposed protocol demonstrates a viable approach to quantum onion routing, contributing to quantum cryptography and network privacy.

title: Excitable Quantum Systems: The Bosonic Avalanche Laser
authors: Louis Garbe And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Louis Garbe and Peter Rabl

We investigate the dynamics of a lasing system driven by a current of bosonic (quasi-)particles via a dissipative three-mode mixing process. A semiclassical analysis of this system predicts distinct dynamical regimes, where both the cavity mode and the gain medium can undergo lasing transitions. Of …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013723] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a bosonic avalanche laser driven by a current of bosonic particles, revealing distinct lasing regimes via semiclassical analysis.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of a lasing system driven by a bosonic current, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors perform a semiclassical analysis of a dissipative three-mode mixing process, deriving equations of motion and identifying dynamical regimes.
result: They find that both the cavity mode and the gain medium can undergo lasing transitions, leading to distinct dynamical phases.
conclusion: The bosonic avalanche laser exhibits rich nonlinear dynamics, potentially useful for quantum information and thermodynamics applications.

title: Berry's Phase On Photonic Quantum Computers
authors: Steven Abel, Iwo Wasek, And Simon Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Abel, Iwo Wasek, and Simon Williams

We formulate a continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) algorithm to study Berry's phase on photonic quantum computers. We demonstrate that CVQC allows the simulation of charged particles with orbital angular momentum under the influence of an adiabatically changing [MATH] field. Alth…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012461] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable quantum computing algorithm to simulate Berry's phase for charged particles with orbital angular momentum in an adiabatically changing magnetic field, demonstrating a new application of photonic quantum computers.
motivation: To explore the use of photonic quantum computers for simulating geometric phases, which are fundamental in quantum mechanics and have applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors formulate a CVQC algorithm that maps the problem of a charged particle with OAM in a magnetic field to a photonic quantum circuit, using continuous-variable operations to simulate the adiabatic evolution.
result: The algorithm successfully simulates Berry's phase, showing that photonic quantum computers can be used to study geometric phases in a controlled manner.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a novel application of CVQC to quantum simulation of geometric phases, potentially useful for quantum information tasks such as holonomic quantum computation.

title: Quantum Optimal Control Of $\mathrm{Λ}$-system Ensembles
authors: Julia Cen And Domenico D'alessandro
abstract:
Author(s): Julia Cen and Domenico D'Alessandro

The quantum [MATH] system is a ubiquitous structure in many quantum technologies, where two stable, lower-energy levels are coupled indirectly via an unstable, higher-energy level that is much more susceptible to decoherence and relaxation. In this paper, we solve the problem of finding a cont…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012623] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method for optimal control of ensembles of Λ-systems, which are common in quantum technologies, by solving the problem of finding a control that drives the system to a desired state while minimizing a cost functional.
motivation: Λ-systems are ubiquitous in quantum technologies, but their control is challenging due to the unstable intermediate level. The authors aim to provide a systematic method for optimal control of such ensembles.
method: The authors formulate the control problem as an optimal control problem for the ensemble of Λ-systems, likely using geometric control theory or Pontryagin's maximum principle to derive the optimal control laws.
result: The paper provides a solution to the optimal control problem for Λ-system ensembles, potentially yielding explicit control strategies that minimize a cost functional while achieving the desired state transfer.
conclusion: The work contributes to the control of hybrid quantum systems, specifically addressing the practical challenge of controlling Λ-systems, which are relevant for quantum information processing and quantum technologies.

title: From Local Weight Selection To Zeno Slowdown In An Open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain With A Single Local Loss
authors: Y. T. Wang And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. T. Wang and X. Z. Zhang

We study a quadratic open SSH chain with a single-site loss and show that the many-body fermionic Lindblad problem admits an exact reduction to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. Its rapidities generate the complete Liouvillian spectrum and reveal three mechan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012457] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an open SSH chain with local loss, showing exact reduction to a non-Hermitian one-body matrix and revealing Zeno slowdown mechanisms.
motivation: To understand the interplay of topology, dissipation, and quantum Zeno effect in a many-body fermionic system, which is relevant to open quantum systems and thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a quadratic open SSH chain with single-site loss, reducing the many-body Lindblad problem to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity, and compute its rapidities to obtain the Liouvillian spectrum.
result: They identify three mechanisms leading to Zeno slowdown, and the exact reduction allows complete characterization of the Liouvillian spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable model for studying dissipation-induced phenomena in topological systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Analysis Of The Action Of Conventional Trapped-ion Entangling Gates In Qudit Space
authors: Pavel A. Kamenskikh, Nikita V. Semenin, Ilia V. Zalivako, Vasiliy N. Smirnov, Ilya A. Semerikov, Ksenia Yu. Khabarova, And Nikolay N. Kolachevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel A. Kamenskikh, Nikita V. Semenin, Ilia V. Zalivako, Vasiliy N. Smirnov, Ilya A. Semerikov, Ksenia Yu. Khabarova, and Nikolay N. Kolachevsky

Qudits, or multilevel quantum information carriers, present a promising path for scaling quantum computers. However, their use introduces increased complexity in quantum logic, necessitating careful control of relative phases between different qudit levels. In trapped-ion systems, entangling operati…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012458] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the action of conventional trapped-ion entangling gates in qudit space, focusing on phase control and gate fidelity for multilevel quantum information carriers.
motivation: Qudits offer a promising path for scaling quantum computers but introduce complexity in quantum logic, requiring careful control of relative phases between qudit levels. The paper aims to understand how standard trapped-ion entangling gates behave when applied to qudits.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the action of conventional trapped-ion entangling gates (such as Mølmer–Sørensen gates) on qudit states, deriving the resulting unitary transformations and phase relationships.
