result: The analysis reveals how the gate operations affect qudit levels, including the generation of relative phases and the conditions for high-fidelity entangling operations in qudit space.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the implementation of entangling gates for trapped-ion qudits, which is important for developing scalable quantum computing with multilevel systems.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Walks On A Defective Lattice: Boosting The Spreading Of Delocalized States Through Parrondo's Strategy
authors: João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, And Edgard P. M. Amorim
abstract:

We investigate the quantum transport of delocalized states in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on a one-dimensional lattice containing a single defect. The defect is modeled by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to the edges that connect the site corresponding to the mean position of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012459] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time quantum walks on a lattice with a defect, using Parrondo's strategy to enhance the spreading of delocalized states.
motivation: Quantum walks are fundamental for quantum information processing, and understanding how defects affect transport is crucial. The authors aim to control and improve quantum transport in the presence of disorder.
method: They model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect by assigning complex hopping amplitudes to edges connected to the defect site. They apply Parrondo's strategy, which involves alternating between two non-optimal dynamics to achieve a net advantage, to boost the spreading of delocalized states.
result: The study demonstrates that Parrondo's strategy can significantly enhance the spreading of delocalized states in the presence of a defect, overcoming the localization typically induced by defects.
conclusion: The findings provide a novel method to control quantum transport in defective lattices, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum simulation.

title: Enhancing Persistent Heat Current Using Inhomogeneous Magnetization
authors: Md Anwar Hosen And Linxiao Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Md Anwar Hosen and Linxiao Zhu

Nonreciprocal many-body systems have been predicted to support various novel phenomena of heat transfer. Persistent heat current represents striking heat flow at thermal equilibrium among at least three nonreciprocal bodies. However, the directionality of the persistent heat current, defined as the …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024314] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that inhomogeneous magnetization can enhance persistent heat currents in nonreciprocal many-body systems at thermal equilibrium.
motivation: Persistent heat currents in nonreciprocal systems are novel but often weak; enhancing them is crucial for practical applications in thermal management and energy conversion.
method: The authors analyze a three-body nonreciprocal system with inhomogeneous magnetization, using theoretical models to compute heat currents and explore parameter dependence.
result: They find that inhomogeneous magnetization can significantly enhance the persistent heat current, with the enhancement depending on system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to boost persistent heat currents, advancing the understanding and control of heat flow in nonreciprocal many-body systems.

title: Attention In Krylov Space: Transformer-based Extrapolation Of Lanczos Coefficients
authors: Zihao Qi And Christopher Earls
abstract:

The Universal Operator Growth Hypothesis formulates the time evolution of operators through Lanczos coefficients. In practice, however, numerical instability and memory cost limit the number of coefficients that can be exactly computed. In response to these challenges, the standard approach relies o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014319] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a transformer-based model to extrapolate Lanczos coefficients in Krylov space, addressing numerical instability and memory constraints in computing operator growth.
motivation: The Universal Operator Growth Hypothesis relies on Lanczos coefficients, but exact computation is limited by numerical instability and memory. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by predicting coefficients beyond the computable range.
method: They employ a transformer architecture trained on exactly computed Lanczos coefficients to extrapolate further coefficients, leveraging attention mechanisms to capture patterns in the sequence.
result: The method successfully predicts Lanczos coefficients with improved accuracy and stability compared to standard approaches, enabling longer-time evolution simulations.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the potential of machine learning, specifically transformers, to extend quantum many-body calculations, offering a practical tool for studying operator growth and dynamics.

title: Optimal Majoranas In Mesoscopic Kitaev Chains

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034512] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal conditions for Majorana zero modes in mesoscopic Kitaev chains realized with quantum dots and superconducting segments, focusing on sweet spots and subgap state effects.
motivation: To understand and optimize the emergence of Majorana zero modes in hybrid quantum dot-superconductor systems, which are promising for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze a Kitaev chain model with quantum dots coupled via superconducting segments, considering subgap states in the hybrid region and their influence on the effective coupling and sweet spots.
result: They identify optimal parameter regimes for robust Majorana zero modes, showing how subgap states can be tuned to enhance the topological phase and improve the quality of the Majoranas.
conclusion: The findings provide practical guidance for engineering mesoscopic Kitaev chains with improved Majorana properties, advancing the feasibility of topological qubits.

title: Theory Of Single-molecule Nmr Detected By Real-time Esr

tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for detecting NMR oscillations in real-time ESR data, relevant to hybrid quantum systems involving spin ensembles and microwave detection.
motivation: Recent experiments have observed NMR oscillations in real-time ESR, but a theoretical understanding is lacking. The authors aim to provide a framework to demonstrate the feasibility of detecting sharp NMR oscillations in such data.
method: The authors develop a theory framework that models the coupled electron-nuclear spin system and the ESR detection process, analyzing the conditions under which NMR oscillations can be resolved in real-time ESR measurements.
result: The framework shows that sharp NMR oscillations can be detected under realistic experimental conditions, providing a theoretical basis for the experimental observations.
conclusion: The work supports the feasibility of single-molecule NMR detection via real-time ESR, contributing to the characterization of hybrid quantum systems involving spin ensembles and microwave detection.

title: Entangled Criticality And Irreversibility In Random Markov Dynamics
authors: Faheem Mosam And Eric de Giuli

motivation: To understand the interplay between criticality and irreversibility in stochastic dynamics, and to explore entanglement properties in such non-equilibrium settings.
method: The authors extend a heterogeneous Markov ensemble by incorporating correlations between forward and backward transition rates, and analyze the resulting dynamics using information-theoretic and thermodynamic measures.
result: They find that the model exhibits critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, leading to non-trivial entanglement and irreversibility properties.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena with information-theoretic tools, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Maximum Entropy Distributions Of Wave Functions At Thermal Equilibrium

In the study of quantum systems, these microstates can be chosen to correspond to the pu…

tldr: This paper derives maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, connecting statistical mechanics with quantum state distributions.
motivation: To understand how quantum microstates are distributed at thermal equilibrium, potentially linking statistical mechanics with quantum information concepts.
method: The authors likely use maximum entropy principles applied to wave functions, possibly within a quantum statistical mechanics framework.
result: They obtain specific distributions for wave functions at thermal equilibrium, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for describing quantum thermal states via maximum entropy, relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Convection Patterns In Nonequilibrium Kawasaki Dynamics At Low Temperature

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014147] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a conservative stochastic lattice gas (Kawasaki dynamics) under a temperature gradient, revealing convection patterns in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic temperature gradients affect phase separation in a stochastic lattice gas, going beyond uniform temperature studies.
method: The authors analyze a Kawasaki dynamics model coupled to a heat bath, using theoretical and possibly numerical methods to characterize the nonequilibrium steady state.
result: They find that a temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with convection patterns, altering the usual phase separation behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium thermodynamics of lattice gases, relevant to understanding transport and pattern formation in driven systems.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators

tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of encoding qudits into qubits and avoiding unphysical states.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding these into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) that uses a specific encoding of spin-1 and spin-3/2 systems into qubits, and they design a cost function that penalizes unphysical states to guide the optimization.
result: The method successfully simulates higher-spin systems, achieving accurate ground state energies for small systems and demonstrating robustness against noise in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed variational approach provides a practical way to simulate higher-spin systems on current qubit-based quantum hardware, expanding the applicability of quantum simulators.

title: Dipolar Optimal Control Of Entangled Current States

method: The authors apply quantum optimal control techniques to exploit dipolar interactions of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring.
result: They demonstrate the generation of selected states with entangled circulation, showing the effectiveness of optimal control.
conclusion: The scheme provides a viable approach for controlling entangled current states, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state method for simulating decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics, using collision quantum optics and density matrices.
motivation: Waveguide QED systems are important for quantum networks, but decoherence is often neglected in simulations. The authors aim to provide a practical method to include decoherence in such calculations.
method: The method uses matrix product states (MPS) and collision quantum optics, representing the waveguide's many-body state with discrete time steps and incorporating decoherence via density matrices.
result: The MPS approach efficiently simulates decoherence in waveguide QED, enabling studies of realistic systems with losses and dephasing.
conclusion: The method offers a versatile tool for modeling decoherence in waveguide QED, relevant for quantum network applications.

title: Frequency Comb Behavior Of Time Crystals In An Rf-driven Dissipative Rydberg System

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033115] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates frequency comb formation in a driven dissipative Rydberg system, linking nonlinear oscillator dynamics to time-crystalline behavior.
motivation: To explore emergent nonlinear oscillator behavior in strongly interacting Rydberg vapors, potentially revealing new aspects of time crystals and synchronization in nonequilibrium systems.
method: The authors study a cesium Rydberg vapor under coherent optical excitation and RF driving, analyzing the system's response to observe frequency comb formation and time-crystal-like behavior.
result: They observe frequency comb behavior, indicating synchronization and nonlinear dynamics in the dissipative Rydberg system, which may be interpreted as a time crystal phase.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying time crystals and nonlinear dynamics in dissipative quantum systems, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Berry-phase-induced Canonical Structure Of Quantum Fluctuations Across The Mott-superfluid Phase Diagram
authors: Idan S. Wallerstein And Eytan Grosfeld
abstract:

We show that commonly used cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state fail in the superfluid phase not only quantitatively but also funda…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033116] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition, revealing a Berry-phase-induced canonical structure of quantum fluctuations.
motivation: To understand the failure of cumulant expansions in the superfluid phase and to provide a correct low-energy description of the Bose-Hubbard model across the phase transition.
method: The authors develop a field-theoretical approach that incorporates Berry phase effects, going beyond standard cumulant expansions, to describe quantum fluctuations in both the Mott and superfluid phases.
result: They show that cumulant expansions fail in the superfluid phase and that a Berry-phase-induced canonical structure correctly captures the low-energy dynamics, providing a unified description across the transition.
conclusion: The work offers a new theoretical framework for the Bose-Hubbard model that may have implications for understanding quantum phase transitions and thermodynamics of correlated systems.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix

tldr: This paper introduces a reinforcement-learning algorithm to find fixed points of quantum operations, which are related to eigenstates of quantum channels.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their long-time behavior, with applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.
method: The algorithm iteratively constructs a unitary transformation mapping the computational basis to the fixed-point basis using a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for broader applications.
conclusion: The reinforcement-learning approach offers a novel computational tool for studying quantum channels and their fixed points, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator

tldr: This paper proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator coupled to a two-level atom, enabling directional quantum light sources.
motivation: Nonreciprocal photon sources are crucial for quantum networks and information processing, but multiphoton bundle emission with nonreciprocity remains challenging.
method: The system uses a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, exploiting the spinning-induced nonreciprocity to achieve directional multiphoton bundle emission.
result: The scheme efficiently generates nonreciprocal multiphoton bundles, with the direction and bundle size controllable by system parameters.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach for realizing nonreciprocal multiphoton sources, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding

tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using the sorted-list encoding, focusing on resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation for chemical systems requires efficient Hamiltonian simulation, and the choice of encoding scheme significantly impacts resource costs. The authors aim to evaluate the sorted-list encoding as a practical option.
method: They analyze the sorted-list encoding for representing fermionic Hamiltonians, comparing its resource requirements (qubits, gates, etc.) against other encodings in the context of quantum phase estimation.
result: The paper provides detailed resource estimates and benchmarks, showing that sorted-list encoding offers advantages in certain regimes, potentially reducing the overall cost of quantum simulation.
conclusion: Sorted-list encoding is a viable and efficient approach for quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:

tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes, providing a universal signature of quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of statistical mechanics. The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic, but its analytic form beyond leading order was not fully known.
method: The authors employ analytical techniques, likely including diagrammatic or field-theoretic methods, to compute the spectral form factor for chaotic many-body systems, considering all Dyson symmetry classes (orthogonal, unitary, symplectic).
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order in time, revealing universal features and symmetry-class-dependent corrections.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and its signatures, with implications for thermalization and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.

tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase observable only through joint measurement.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, and its experimental realization in a controllable platform like trapped ions is of high interest.
method: The authors engineer dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, and they measure the synchronized state via joint measurements that reveal the fixed relative phase.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement, confirming the quantum nature of the synchronization.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems, though it is not a core focus of the user's interests.

result: They show that tensor-network process tensors can efficiently simulate diverse physical scenarios, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics settings.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability in quantum information and thermodynamics.

result: The proposed method successfully certifies quantum non-Gaussian light in a loss-invariant manner, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying non-classicality and non-Gaussianity, which is valuable for quantum information processing and quantum optics.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik

tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that inject auxiliary terms to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with minimal cost increase, reducing circuit depth for target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is crucial for quantum algorithms, but product formulas often require high circuit depth for accurate simulation. The authors aim to improve the efficiency of product formulas by adding carefully designed auxiliary terms.
method: The authors propose a method to correct product formulas by injecting auxiliary terms that cancel leading error terms, thereby enhancing accuracy without substantial overhead. They analyze the error scaling and demonstrate improvements in circuit depth.
result: The corrected product formulas achieve a target accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical way to enhance Hamiltonian simulation efficiency, which is beneficial for quantum algorithms and aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum information processing.

authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.

method: They propose adding cluster corrections to belief propagation, which account for correlations beyond local neighborhoods, and derive rigorous bounds on the approximation error.
result: The method achieves exponential convergence to the exact contraction value with increasing cluster size, and demonstrates improved accuracy over standard belief propagation on benchmark problems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximate tensor network contraction, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, offering unique benefits for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation.

authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array in a cryogenic environment extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, thereby reducing errors in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg lifetimes, which are degraded by blackbody radiation at room temperature. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic apparatus to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, and measure Rydberg lifetimes and gate fidelities at low temperatures.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes and a corresponding reduction in relaxation errors, leading to improved two-qubit gate fidelities.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable and effective strategy to mitigate Rydberg decay errors, advancing the performance of neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in continual quantum learning, showing that quantum neural networks maintain adaptability as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer inherent advantages in preserving plasticity.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, comparing plasticity retention with classical counterparts.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, enabling long-term learning without explicit regularization.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks could provide a robust framework for continual learning, leveraging quantum properties to maintain adaptability.

method: They decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a photonic simulator that can be configured for various simulations.
result: The approach allows for efficient execution of simulation algorithms, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator offers a practical and configurable platform for studying quantum field dynamics, potentially advancing quantum simulation.

tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for benchmarking quantum advantage experiments.
method: The authors analyze the statistical properties of output distributions of random circuits under local noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They identify distinct depth regimes where anticoncentration behaves differently, and show that the onset of anticoncentration is universal across different circuit architectures, depending only on the noise rate and depth.
conclusion: The findings provide a robust framework for predicting when noisy quantum circuits lose their computational advantage, with implications for quantum supremacy experiments and error mitigation.

result: The implementation successfully approximates the Jones polynomial for small knots, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach. The results show that the quantum algorithm can outperform classical methods for certain instances, indicating potential quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete quantum algorithm for a mathematically significant problem, providing a new benchmark for quantum computers and highlighting areas where quantum advantage may be achievable.

tldr: This paper demonstrates that collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters can enhance photon blockade, leading to stronger antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade is typically limited by the need for strong single-emitter nonlinearities. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting collective effects in an ensemble, which could enable more practical quantum devices.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a model of an ensemble of emitters coupled to a cavity, focusing on two-photon interactions. They derive conditions for photon blockade and study how collective effects scale with the number of emitters.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, with antibunching improving as the system size increases, while maintaining high transmission. This occurs even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a new mechanism for achieving strong photon blockade, which could be useful for quantum information processing and photonic quantum technologies.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. The paper aims to unify diverse time-propagation techniques to facilitate understanding and comparison.
method: The authors present a unified framework that categorizes and relates different simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: The paper offers a comprehensive overview of methods, including their applicability and limitations, across multiple fields such as quantum thermodynamics and quantum information.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation techniques for non-Markovian dynamics, advancing both theoretical and practical aspects of open quantum systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review explores space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, connecting brickwork quantum circuits to solvable dynamics and quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the review aims to provide a unified pedagogical view using space-time duality.
method: The review synthesizes recent advances in discretizing time evolution on lattices, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their space-time dual interpretation.
result: It presents a unified framework for exactly solvable many-body dynamics, highlighting the analogy with quantum computation and the role of special lattice structures.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful perspective for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with implications for quantum simulation and computation.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the Toffoli gate with qutrits.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages in quantum computing, such as reducing circuit complexity and enabling more efficient algorithms, but their role is not as well understood as qubits.
method: The paper surveys various qudit-qubit embeddings, discusses theoretical frameworks for gate decomposition using qudits, and reviews current experimental implementations.
result: It demonstrates that qudits can simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and provides an overview of experimental progress in qudit-based quantum computing.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum information processing, with potential for simplifying circuits and enabling new algorithms, though practical challenges remain.

title: Sub-Hertz Optical Transitions In Excited ${\mathrm{Yb}}^{+}$
authors: Patrick Mcmillin, Hassan Farhat, William Liu, And Wesley C. Campbell

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel quantum phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear driving and mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution.
result: Highlights mechanisms for metastable and nonthermal states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.
conclusion: Photoexcitation of Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium quantum phenomena, but the paper is primarily a review without new technical results.

result: DQPTs remain robust under slow quenching, but their characteristics (e.g., critical times) change with quench rate.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition and scope of active matter, including recent developments like quantum active matter, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

method: The paper provides a historical and conceptual review, offering a definition of active matter and surveying recent topics such as nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
result: The paper proposes a precise definition of active matter and highlights emerging subfields, including quantum active matter.
conclusion: Active matter is a distinct subset of nonequilibrium systems, and its study may intersect with quantum physics, but this paper is primarily a conceptual review without direct relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review covers tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution, a technique in nanoscale optical imaging.
motivation: To provide an overview of a scanning probe technique that combines optical fluorescence with atomic-scale resolution, which is important for studying molecular structures.
method: The paper is a review article summarizing the principles and recent advances in tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy.
result: It discusses how the scanning tip acts as an optical antenna to confine electromagnetic fields, enabling superresolution imaging down to the atomic scale.
conclusion: The technique offers new insights into molecular identification and submolecular structures, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This review paper discusses the fundamental mechanisms of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Understanding vacuum breakdown is crucial for improving the reliability and efficiency of particle accelerators and other high-power technologies.
method: The paper synthesizes recent experimental and simulation studies to present a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation and evolution.
result: It identifies key factors such as surface defects, electric field enhancement, and thermal effects that trigger breakdown, and highlights advances in predictive modeling.
conclusion: Improved understanding of vacuum breakdown can lead to better design and operation of high-gradient accelerators and other high-voltage vacuum systems.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including magnetism, topology, and dynamics.
motivation: To summarize the rapidly evolving field of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged theories.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes current knowledge on 2D magnets, discussing experimental and theoretical advances across various subfields.
result: The review highlights the breadth of the field, including ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and applications in spintronics and magnonics.
conclusion: The field is actively expanding, with potential for new applications, but the paper does not focus on quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind the wealth of exotic phenomena observed in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and orbital antiferromagnetism.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, discussing the role of topology, correlations, and spin-orbit coupling.
result: It highlights the emergence of topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and various correlated and topological phases in kagome metals.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for exploring novel quantum states, but the paper does not directly contribute to the user's specified research directions.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for chemical, ecological, and epidemiological modeling.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for analyzing complex systems modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, which are prevalent in biology, sociology, and traffic flow.
method: The review synthesizes field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and quantum methods, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: It demonstrates how diverse models can be unified under a single field-theoretic framework, offering a comprehensive pedagogical resource.
conclusion: The paper is a valuable educational review but does not directly contribute to the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes how gravitational-wave and X-ray observations of neutron stars constrain the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial information about the behavior of matter under extreme compression, which is not directly accessible in terrestrial experiments.
method: The paper reviews recent observational results from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, and compares them to theoretical predictions from nuclear equation of state calculations extrapolated to high densities.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and the comparisons with theoretical predictions provide insights into the equation of state at supranuclear densities.
conclusion: The review highlights the current state of knowledge and outlines future observational opportunities to further constrain the dense matter equation of state.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review connects statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to large-scale neural recordings, aiming to uncover reproducible collective behaviors in brain networks.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge theoretical statistical physics with experimental neuroscience to find quantitative principles governing neural network activity.
method: The paper reviews recent work applying maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to multi-neuron recording data.
result: It highlights that these methods reveal reproducible collective behaviors and predictive power in neural data.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for understanding complex neural networks, with potential for further theoretical development.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.

tldr: This review covers the quantum mechanics of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Stellar nuclear reactions are difficult to measure directly, and theoretical understanding is needed to model stellar burning and element formation.

result: It summarizes the state of the art in theoretical nuclear astrophysics and proposes novel methods to study these reactions in the lab.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that apparent violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivations.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how such violations can be exploited to design novel materials.
method: A review of various physical properties and circumstances where measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds, analyzing which underlying assumptions are violated.
result: Identifies multiple cases where apparent violations occur and explains the assumptions violated, also discussing how to design materials that intentionally violate these assumptions.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are due to assumption violations, and understanding this can lead to materials with interesting properties.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses self-alignment in active matter systems, a topic in soft matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to unify the concept of self-alignment in active matter, which is a key mechanism in biological and robotic systems, but it is outside the user's research interests.

conclusion: Self-alignment is a powerful principle in active matter, but it does not align with the user's focus on quantum information and related fields.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.

This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. abstract:

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.

conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly could challenge the standard ΛCDM model, but further investigation is needed to rule out systematic effects and confirm the anomaly.

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark matter halo dynamics and large-scale structure, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize current knowledge and observational constraints on self-interacting dark matter, a topic in cosmology and particle physics.
method: It is a review article that synthesizes theoretical models and astrophysical observations, including galaxy dynamics and large-scale structure.
result: The review presents the current status of self-interacting dark matter constraints and highlights future observational prospects.
conclusion: The paper concludes that self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and future surveys expected to improve constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, and the paper aims to assess its viability and discovery potential at the HL-LHC.
method: The paper surveys current experimental bounds and theoretical developments, and presents projections for discovery across multiple search channels and scenarios.
result: It provides an outlook on the remaining viable supersymmetric models and their discovery potential at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: The paper concludes that while stringent bounds exist, the HL-LHC offers significant opportunities to discover or further constrain supersymmetry.
